content: Two recent epidemiological studies have indicated that children who use non-feather pillows experience wheezing episodes more frequently compared to those who use feather pillows. The objective of this review was to assess whether feather bedding is effective in controlling asthma symptoms. A search was conducted using the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register with predefined search terms, and the search was updated as of February 2009. The inclusion criteria required randomized or controlled clinical trials. However, no studies meeting these criteria were identified. A total of 15 studies were retrieved and reviewed in full-text form, but none satisfied the entry requirements for this review. While recent epidemiological evidence suggests that feather bedding may be associated with a lower frequency of wheezing compared to synthetic fiber bedding, the currently available evidence is insufficient to determine the clinical benefits of feather bedding in asthma management.
